subject: Post-call: Hearthly benchmark prep & recommended model shortlist
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Gomez <samira.gomez@hearthlyhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Hearthly benchmark prep & recommended model shortlist

Thanks Samira — great conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we kick off the benchmark run: 

Summary of call
- Objective: validate model fit for two production features: (1) discharge-summary classification into 10 clinical categories, and (2) concise post-discharge summary generation (250-400 tokens).
- Success metrics you asked for: label F1 >= 0.88, summarization mean jury score >= 4.2/5, hallucination rate < 2% (defined below).

Redwood recommended shortlist (initial candidates)
- Llama 2 70B — 8-bit quantized (best-in-class accuracy for classification; higher latency/cost).
- Llama 3 13B — 16k context (good balance of summary coherence and throughput).
- redwood/inf-3b-ql8 (production-optimized 3B variant) — fastest for low-latency interactive paths, good baseline for regression checks.

Benchmark artifacts I’m attaching/linked
- hearthly_prompt_bank_v1.csv (attached) — small set (n=250) of representative prompts + expected labels and reference summaries. Columns: id, prompt, reference, category_label, pii_flag, notes.
- hearthly_benchmark_spec_v1.md (attached / Drive link) — run instructions, scoring rubric, and dataset formatting rules.
- Scoring sheet (in Drive) — template for juror scores and automated metrics.

PHI & security note
- For any records containing PHI we recommend either Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS. We can run an initial blind benchmark using deidentified samples you control; later runs can be run in your Private environment.

Proposed next steps
1) You upload a ~2k-sample CSV (schema in spec) to the Drive folder by Wed 2/24 if possible.
2) We (Redwood) run the 3-model shortlist across the sample (batch run) and return: token/time cost table, per-example predictions, and jury-scored sample of 200 generated summaries. Target turnaround: 48-72 hours after sample upload.
3) Joint readout to review model tradeoffs, recommended production configuration (batching, quantization profile, cache keys), and estimated monthly cost for your projected QPS.

If that sounds good I’ll schedule the run and loop in infra for a Dedicated estimate (if you need it). I’ve CC’d Ben and Marissa to coordinate scoring and any post-run remediation/playbook.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189

Attachments: hearthly_prompt_bank_v1.csv (CSV), hearthly_benchmark_spec_v1.md (Markdown)
From: Samira Gomez <samira.gomez@hearthlyhealth.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hearthly Health Procurement <procurement@hearthlyhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Hearthly benchmark prep & recommended model shortlist

Thanks Karthik — this is exactly the kind of clarity we needed. A few quick questions before we upload the sample: 

1) PHI handling: for the trial run you proposed, can Redwood guarantee no human access to raw inputs? We need an attestation for our security team; if not, we’ll deidentify records first.
2) Scoring thresholds: our clinical reviewers prefer to see an automated hallucination flag in the results (e.g., model output contains new medical facts not present in the reference). Can you include an automated hallucination heuristic in the output payload?
3) Data format: our data team uses NDJSON exports. The attached sample they produced uses id/prompt/reference fields but also a nested metadata object — can you confirm Redwood’s runner accepts NDJSON or do you prefer flat CSV?

Procurement loop: procurement@hearthlyhealth.com — they’ll need a short SOW and an estimate if we proceed with Dedicated or Private.

I’ll aim to upload a deidentified 2k sample by Wed EOD if the answers above look good.

Best,
Samira
Director, Clinical ML — Hearthly Health
samira.gomez@hearthlyhealth.com

Hi Samira — quick answers and implementation notes: 

1) Human access & PHI
- Attestation: for Hosted runs we cannot guarantee zero human access (operations-level access is controlled and audited). For PHI we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS and strict RBAC; both provide no-human-inspection contractual language in our SOW for sensitive workloads. I’ve added Procurement on the thread.

2) Automated hallucination heuristic
- Yes — our benchmark runner can compute two signals: (a) token-overlap based hallucination flag (low overlap + novel medical entities), and (b) an entity-consistency heuristic that checks extracted entities against the reference. We’ll include per-example flags and a hallucination_rate aggregate. Details are in the benchmark spec (attached).

3) Dataset format
- Preferred: flat CSV or NDJSON where each line maps to id, prompt, reference, category_label, pii_flag, source_timestamp. We cannot accept nested JSON objects for the reference cell — please flatten metadata into separate columns (e.g., device:..., encounter_type:...). If your export is NDJSON we can accept it as long as each top-level record is flat.

Run logistics & scoring criteria (summary)
- Automated metrics: per-class precision/recall/F1, token-level perplexity, ROUGE-L and BERTScore for summarization, hallucination_rate (automated).
- Human jurors: 5-judge average for fluency/coherence (1-5), domain accuracy (1-5), and a binary safety flag.
- Pass thresholds we’ll flag in the readout: label F1 >= 0.88, jury mean >= 4.2, hallucination_rate < 2%. These are guidance — we’ll show tradeoffs at readout.

Timing & deliverables
- If you upload by Wed EOD (2/24) we’ll run the shortlist and deliver a results bundle within 72 hours: per-example outputs, summary metrics, cost/time table, and a recommendation deck.
- If you want the run inside Private/Dedicated we’ll produce a short SOW and cost estimate within 48 hours after you confirm environment preference.

Next step: please confirm upload format and whether you want the run in Hosted (deidentified data) or Private/Dedicated (PHI). I’ll provision the runner and schedule the job.

Thanks — Karthik

[Attachment: hearthly_benchmark_spec_v1.md — contains the automated hallucination heuristic and scoring templates]
